name: Question 2
problem:
Let $f(x,y)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,-1)=-2,\,{f}_{x}(x,y)=2xy-{y}^{2},\,{f}_{y}(x,y)={x}^{2}-2xy.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,-1),$ estimate the value of $f(0.95,-1.04).$
worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(1,-1)+∇f(1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-(-1)⟩ \\  & ≈f(1,-1)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,-1),{f}_{y}(1,-1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1⟩ \\  & ≈-2+⟨{f}_{x}(1,-1),{f}_{y}(1,-1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(1,-1)$ and ${f}_{y}(1,-1)$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,-1) & =2(1)(-1)-(-1)^{2}=-3 \\ {f}_{y}(1,-1) & ={1}^{2}-2(1)(-1)=3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)≈-2+⟨-3,3⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(0.95,-1.04)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=0.95$ and $y=-1.04,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.95,-1.04) & ≈-2+⟨-3,3⟩\cdot ⟨0.95-1,-1.04+1⟩ \\  & =-2+⟨-3,3⟩\cdot ⟨-0.05,-0.04⟩ \\  & =-2-3(-0.05)+3(-0.04) \\  & =-2+0.15-0.12 \\  & =-1.97\end{aligned}
$$
